title: First-principles DFT study of the structural, electronic and vibrational properties of azidopentazole
authors: Kortus J., Pederson M.R., Richardson S.L.
notes_general: This paper recomputes two ALREADY-KNOWN N8 topologies (azidopentazole Cs, octaazapentalene D2h) at a different level of theory (all-electron PBE/NRLMOL) purely as a cross-validation exercise -- both topologies already exist in the current corpus as molecules.py ids 'N8_Cs_azidopentazole' and 'N8_D2h_pentalene' (both originally from poly-N.pdf/Glukhovtsev et al. B3LYP/6-31G*). The paper itself states its PBE bond lengths/angles agree with the existing B3LYP values within 0.1 A / 1 deg. Figure 1 (azidopentazole) and Figure 2 (octaazapentalene) DO show fully bond-length/angle-labeled 2D diagrams, but atom-index correspondence is not printed on the figure (no atom numbering), so precise per-bond transcription was not attempted here given the topology is already exactly reconstructed elsewhere in the corpus -- not worth the transcription-error risk for a duplicate. This paper's main NEW contribution is IR/Raman vibrational spectra for azidopentazole (Table 2: 17 modes from 54 to 2164 cm-1, IR intensities, Raman activities) -- useful for future spectroscopic validation but not a new geometry.

bond_params.shape: 5-membered pentazole ring with 3-atom azide-like tail (same topology as existing N8_Cs_azidopentazole)

species.notes: E=-437.56550 Ha, E0(ZPE-corrected)=-437.53077 Ha, decomposition energy to 4N2 = 171.9 kcal/mol (PBE). Authors' own bond lengths/angles (Fig. 1, legible but no atom-index labels) agree with Glukhovtsev B3LYP/6-31G* (already in corpus) within 0.1 A / 1 deg per their own comparison -- treat as a validated duplicate, not a new topology. Vertical IP=10.9 eV, electron affinity=0.63 eV, HOMO=-7.6 eV, LUMO=-4.136 eV. Full IR/Raman spectrum in Table 2 (17 modes, 54-2164 cm-1) -- strongest IR mode 2164 cm-1 (369.5 km/mol), useful for spectroscopic cross-check if a relaxed structure is later computed.

bond_params.shape: two fused five-membered rings (pentalene-like), same topology as existing N8_D2h_pentalene

species.notes: E=-437.54780 Ha, E0=-437.51182 Ha, decomposition energy to 4N2 = 183.8 kcal/mol (PBE). Cited as the lowest-energy N8 isomer in a 10-isomer study by Gagliardi et al. (not in this archive), but this paper finds azidopentazole is lower in energy than octaazapentalene at PBE level -- consistent ordering with existing corpus.
